source.title: MURANO: Design, Run, and Reproduce Mechanistic Interpretability Experiments as Composable Pipelines
source.authors: Alireza Bayat Makou; Emirhan Böge; Phu Gia Hoang; Federico Tiblias; Jing-Cheng Niu; Subhabrata Dutta; Richard Eckart de Castilho; Iryna Gurevych

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports an IOI reproduction on GPT-2 small, using corrupted-output patching and the IO logit difference to test selected reported head roles.
record.gate_note: The IOI results in Section 5.1 bear on the claim. The truth-direction and SAE case studies, framework comparisons, and cited results from Wang et al. are not rows. The paper explicitly cautions that attention and output-projection measurements do not establish that a head copied the answer in the original forward pass.
record.test_reason: Section 5.1 reproduces selected IOI findings on GPT-2 small with corrupted-prompt head patching and the IO-minus-S logit difference. These are the original's method and metric, and the study is not an original source. Its outputs bear on V1 (head roles) and partly on V5 (ablation dependence).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The head sweep recovers the three reported name movers and the two negative movers, and the S-inhibition query result holds for two of three name movers. The mean-ablation caveat (not necessary for the answer) comes from Section 5.1 rather than the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: It uses GPT-2 small, clean and corrupted IOI prompts, head-output patching, and an IO logit-difference score, but reports a selected head sweep and selected patches rather than the full circuit criteria. The reported sweep leaves MLP outputs unfrozen.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported effects vary by patch type (query versus value) and target name-mover head. The paper says its case studies use fixed prompt sets and do not systematically test sensitivity to alternative samples or hyperparameters.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
record.problems: The IOI study reports a fixed prompt setup and no uncertainty estimates. It does not systematically test alternative prompt samples or hyperparameters. MLP outputs are not frozen in the head sweep and may carry part of the resulting change. Attention and output-projection measurements do not establish copying in the original forward pass.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit (duplicate-token, induction, previous-token, S-inhibition as nodes, backup name movers) and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Whether backup heads take over after name-mover ablation. r14 shows no LD drop, but no head is shown compensating.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse.
Other circuit-finding methods or metrics recovering the circuit.
Prompt-distribution sensitivity, metric choice, and the fraction of behaviour explained by the full circuit.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tooling demo paper whose IOI part is a partial reproduction. The sweep leaves MLPs unfrozen, and the numeric sweep effects appear only in the notebooks, not the text. No uncertainty is reported and prompts are fixed. The truth-direction and SAE studies are irrelevant to this claim.

versions.untested_parts: The complete 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not tested. Only selected head rankings, selected S-inhibition patches, and mean ablation of the three reported name-mover heads are reported.
Whether identified backup heads take over the main name-mover role after ablation.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of components for other tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
Prompt-distribution sensitivity and a systematic comparison of circuit faithfulness or completeness across metrics are not tested.
Other name orders, templates, and prompts with more names.

rows.check: Link V5 as well: final-token path patching with other heads frozen shows L9H9 as strongly important, while mean ablation (r14) shows no drop. That contrast is an ablation-type dependence. No number is given in the text, only the rank.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Mean ablation of the three reported name-mover heads.
rows.measure: Mean correct indirect-object logit minus distractor-subject logit
rows.note: The authors state that this result does not show the name-mover heads are necessary for the answer.
rows.check: Mean ablation raises LD slightly (3.484 to 3.520), so there is no necessity effect for V1. For V5 the same row shows that name-mover importance depends on ablation type, contrasting with r1-r3. It is consistent with backup compensation (V2), but backup heads are not measured, so it cannot be linked to V2.

source_check.correct: Logit difference changes from 3.484 to 3.520. V1: absent necessity effect under joint mean ablation. V5: observed intervention dependence when compared with r1-r3; use version-specific states.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, mean-ablation result and preceding head-sweep results.
source_check.problem: The shared absent state fits the V1 necessity result but not the observed V5 intervention dependence.

relationships.condition: Final-token corrupted head sweep, IO attention, output projection, S-inhibition query patches to L9H9 and L10H0, value patches
relationships.reason: The reported name movers and negative movers rank as the top effects (r1-r5). Two of the heads attend strongly to IO (r6, r7). Names copy at 96-100% (r9). Query patches lower LD by 28.9% and 22.8% of the gap (r10, r11). Value patches have no effect, as in the original (r13).
relationships.display_finding: Name movers and negative movers had the largest effects, two heads attended strongly to IO, name copying reached 96–100%, query patches reduced logit difference by 28.9% and 22.8% of the gap, and value patches had no effect.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Final-token corrupted head sweep, IO attention, output projection, S-inhibition query patches to L9H9 and L10H0, value patches
source_check.reason: r1-r7 recover the reported head rankings and attention patterns; r9 establishes copying tendency; r10-r11 have the expected query-patch direction; r13 reproduces the null value-patch result. These support selected roles, without validating the whole circuit.

relationships.condition: S-inhibition query patch targeting name mover L9H6
relationships.reason: The query patch raises LD by 4.9% of the gap, opposite to the reported S-inhibition role; the authors state it holds for only two of three heads (r12).
relationships.display_finding: The query patch increased logit difference by 4.9% of the gap, reversing the expected effect; the authors reported the proposed effect for only two of three heads.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: S-inhibition query patch targeting name mover L9H6
source_check.reason: r12 raises logit difference by 4.9% of the clean-to-corrupt gap, reversing the expected direction; the authors explicitly report successful S-inhibition reproduction for only two of three tested name movers.

relationships.condition: Mean ablation of the three name movers; L10H0 attention
relationships.reason: Mean ablation leaves LD unchanged (3.484 to 3.520), so the heads are not shown to be necessary (r14). L10H0 IO attention is weaker at 0.460 (r8).
relationships.display_finding: Ablating the three name movers changed logit difference from 3.484 to 3.520, providing no necessity evidence, while L10H0 attended to IO with weight 0.460.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Mean ablation of the three name movers; L10H0 attention
source_check.reason: r8 shows substantially weaker IO attention for L10H0 than for the other two name movers. r14 does not establish joint necessity under mean ablation. These qualify the selected head-role evidence without establishing failure of the entire 26-head circuit.

relationships.condition: Final-token path patching versus mean ablation of name movers
relationships.reason: The same heads are the strongest effects under frozen-head patching (r1-r3) but show no LD drop under mean ablation (r14). Their apparent importance depends on the ablation used.
relationships.display_finding: The strongest heads under frozen-head patching caused no logit-difference drop under mean ablation.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Final-token path patching versus mean ablation of name movers
source_check.reason: r1-r3 show the strongest negative effects under corrupted-output patching with other heads frozen, whereas r14 shows no logit-difference reduction under joint mean ablation, supporting intervention-dependent apparent importance.

relation.reason: Its own head sweep, query/value patches, attention measurements and mean ablation bear on selected circuit roles and intervention sensitivity.

tranche.reason: The selected reproduction uses corrupted-activation head/path patching and the IO-minus-subject logit difference on GPT-2 small. It reports scientific head-role results as well as demonstrating the framework.

source_check.notes: The head sweep normalizes by the clean score; query-patch percentages normalize by the clean-to-corrupt gap. MLP outputs remain unfrozen in the sweep. Whole-circuit faithfulness, completeness and minimality are untested; review status is supplied metadata, not established by the study text.

statements.correction: Murano: three reported name movers have the strongest negative sweep effects; two reported negative movers have the strongest positive effects; tested name tokens rank among the five highest-scoring output-projection tokens in 96%-100% of cases; causal copying in the original forward pass is not established.
statements.problem: Name copying overstates the output-projection result: the authors explicitly distinguish copying tendency from copying the answer during the original forward pass. The recovery fractions and 30-pair experiment are not attributed to Murano and are outside this study's check.

reader_labels.condition: Reported query patches, value patches, and name-mover mean ablation
reader_labels.reason: Outcomes differ across patch type and target head, and mean ablation leaves the measured logit difference essentially unchanged; prompt-distribution sensitivity is not evaluated (r10-r14).
